rubric.why: A covalent bond forms when atoms share electrons.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as one formed by sharing electrons between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms share electrons to form the bond.

rubric.why: A single covalent bond contains one shared pair of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a single covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

rubric.why: A double covalent bond contains two shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a double covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

rubric.why: A triple covalent bond contains three shared pairs of electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies a triple covalent bond and gives an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the type and a suitable example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
A single covalent bond has one shared pair of electrons; for example, H2.
A double covalent bond has two shared pairs of electrons; for example, O2.
A triple covalent bond has three shared pairs of electrons; for example, N2.

items.followUp: How many particles are present in one mole of a substance? Give the value.

rubric.why: Avogadro’s number is the number of particles in one mole of a substance.
rubric.description: Defines Avogadro’s number as the number of particles in one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a count of particles in one mole.

rubric.why: Nₐ is the symbol for Avogadro’s number; its value is approximately 6.02 × 10²³.
rubric.description: Gives the symbol of Avogadro’s number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the symbol Nₐ; accept the numerical value as an alternative.

modelAnswer: Avogadro’s number is the number of particles present in one mole of a substance.
Its symbol is Nₐ (NA), and its value is 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
